weaknesses: Methodological novelty is limited: the EIG estimator and distinction between mutual information and predictive entropy are established. The distinctive contributions are largely hypothesis filtering, retention, diversity prompting, and conditional question generation, yet these components receive no controlled ablations. The alternative-factorization comparison has a mathematical inconsistency. Appendix C, Equation 8, drops the marginal hypothesis entropy as a design-independent constant, although Section 4.3 correctly notes that this marginal can depend on the question under the data–estimation construction. Without an additional consistency assumption, Algorithm 1 optimizes expected conditional entropy rather than EIG. Figure 4 therefore does not cleanly establish the claimed advantage of factorization under a common information-gain objective.

The connection between the acquisition objective and actual belief updating remains qualitative. Hard rejection, deduplication, uniform weighting, retention, and regeneration do not implement the Bayesian posterior assumed when interpreting EIG as expected uncertainty reduction. Although this mismatch is acknowledged, there is no direct assessment of its consequences, likelihood calibration, or erroneous rejection of the true hypothesis.

External validity is limited. All interactions use LLM answerers, and the preference experiment converts MovieLens ratings into synthetic personas before evaluating recommendations with the answerer itself as an LLM judge. The relatively modest recommendation gains are not validated against held-out human ratings or human judgments. Changing model families provides useful robustness evidence but does not resolve this limitation.

Computational practicality is insufficiently evaluated. The nominal 20-Questions configuration requires approximately 225 question–hypothesis likelihood evaluations per turn, plus generation and historical-consistency checks. No latency, token-cost, or performance–budget analysis is reported. While the Entropy comparison is well controlled, the large gains over single-sample Naive QA do not establish competitiveness against other prompting or search strategies with comparable inference budgets.

Reproducibility and evaluation details are incomplete. The supplied manuscript omits the filtering threshold and exact prompts for the principal method, answerers, and recommendation judge, and provides no implementation link. Section 6.1 also describes greedy decoding as extracting the highest-likelihood hypothesis from a belief distribution previously defined as uniform over retained candidates; the actual prediction rule and its consistent application across baselines need clarification. These omissions materially limit verification of the reported gains.
